card.name: Modal verbs in drug interaction statements
card.fires_on: The small verb right after a drug name, such as may, can, or the to in 'shown to', where the sentence says one drug changes the effect of another. It appears in drug interaction sections.

modes.label: may/can after drug name
modes.description: A modal verb follows a drug name and introduces an increase or decrease in effect.
modes.example: allopurinol<< may>> decrease anti-tumor activity due to suppression

modes.label: shown/known to
modes.description: The word to follows 'shown' or 'known' before a verb describing an interaction effect.
modes.example: Metronidazole was shown<< to>> decrease the clearance of fluorouracil

card.writes: It seems to prepare words about sensitivity and synergy, meaning a drug raises or lowers another's effect.
card.plain: It marks the spot in an interaction sentence where a drug is about to be said to raise or lower another drug's effect.
